optimizedDescription.value: Runs trusted graph-index tasks in a lock-owning child with validated IPC, crash containment, typed failures, and deterministic cleanup.

optimizedContext.value:
# Isolated Index Worker

## Rules
- Public `runIsolatedGraphIndex` accepts storage root, trusted installed task-module URL/absolute path, JSON-serializable input, optional progress callback; resolves JSON-serializable result. No rendering, CLI-format interpretation, host exit-state mutation, or `process.exit()`.
- Acquire shared storage-root index lock before fork. Same-root concurrency fails typed busy before second child. Supervisor owns lease through child lifetime; releases exactly once after success, task failure, creation/IPC/send failure, invalid/duplicate terminal IPC, early/non-zero/signal exit, native crash.
- Startup failure remains bounded without `exit`: detach owned listeners, tear down IPC, best-effort terminate, release once, reject typed startup failure. Lock helpers/tokens remain internal.
- Lock acquisition delegates stale-owner recovery to shared helper from `code-graph:staleness-detection`; supervisor only consumes acquired/typed-busy result and implements no PID recovery.
- Lease-holding process releases on process exit; also Windows `SIGBREAK` and delivered `SIGTERM`. Missing `SIGTERM` delivery cannot leave lease after exit.
- Production uses `node:child_process.fork` with package-shipped worker. Child contains task, parsers, native provider/store work; native crash cannot terminate host.
- Success requires terminal result, task cleanup, then exit code 0; post-result crash/signal remains failure. Cleanup fixes lifecycle faults without `process.exit()`.
- Worker imports exactly host-selected trusted module. Async entrypoint receives serializable input+progress emitter, returns one serializable result or throws. Missing/non-callable entrypoint or non-serializable input/progress/result yields typed task/protocol failure.
- Module selection never end-user CLI input; capability is no untrusted-code sandbox.
- Tagged runtime-validated IPC allows zero-or-more progress then one terminal result/failure. Malformed/unsupported, late, duplicate, or missing terminal state is protocol failure. Never double-settle, signal, or release. Raw envelopes/bootstrap remain internal.
- Forward valid progress unchanged and ordered. Missing callback changes nothing. Child/supervisor emit no CLI-specific text/JSON/TOON; hosts present.
- Typed `SpecdCodeGraphError` failures with stable upper-snake-case codes distinguish busy, fork/IPC startup, invalid module/contract, task failure, malformed/unsupported/late/duplicate IPC, abnormal/early exit, signal termination; include actionable message and structured exit/signal details.
- During child activity install parent `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` handlers, forward same signal, await child, clean up, reject typed signal failure. Remove only installed handlers; never exit/re-signal host.
- Child receives internal storage-root-scoped indication supervisor owns lock; provider skips reacquisition only for matching child/root. No public/caller token or unrelated bypass.
- Build emits stable ESM worker under published `dist/`; supervisor resolves relative to installed package. Verification forks publish-shaped worker/task; built integration forces project index through terminal result, cleanup, exit 0.
- Listener removal, child-reference cleanup, IPC teardown, lock release idempotent and complete before settlement. Leave no lock file, live child, open IPC. Tests may inject launcher/protocol seam; production has no worker-thread/in-process mode.

## Constraints
- Child process mandatory for native-crash containment.
- No queueing, lock waiting, automatic retry, scheduled/background indexing, or local stale-lock/PID recovery.
- No dependency on `@specd/sdk`, `@specd/cli`, Commander, delivery formatter.
- Inputs, progress, results, IPC payloads runtime-validated JSON-serializable at boundary.
- Direct lock helpers/raw IPC DTOs internal.
